title: Hol? or Hová? The question decides

sections.title: One place, two endings
sections.content: Every place word has two forms. Use the *-ban/-ben* form to say where someone is, and the *-ba/-be* form to say where someone is going. The question tells you which: *Hol?* wants *-ban/-ben*, *Hová?* wants *-ba/-be*. The vowel rule and the lengthened *-a/-e* are the same in both forms: *kávézó* gives *kávézóban* and *kávézóba*; *mozi* gives *moziban* and *moziba*.

items.spanish: Hol van Anna? Az irodában van.
items.english: Where is Anna? She is in the office.

items.spanish: Hová megy Anna? Az irodába megy.
items.english: Where is Anna going? She is going to the office.
Where are you? I am at the cinema.
Where are you going? I am going to the cinema.

sections.content: Hear the *-n* at the end. If the answer to the question ends in *-n*, the person is already there. If it ends in the vowel, the person is on the way. *Az étteremben van* and *Az étterembe megy* describe two different moments.
